title: The Effect of a Butyrate-enhancing Synbiotic Intervention on Inflammatory Depression: A Stratified, Double-Blind, Randomized Controlled Trial (BEYOND DEPRESSION)
summary: Approximately 25 % of people suffering from major depression are affected by chronic, low-grade inflammation. It is believed that this is associated with a change in the gut microbiome characterized by a reduced number of beneficial bacteria. These bacteria produce certain metabolites, known as short-chain fatty acids, which have a strong anti-inflammatory effect and may therefore be present in lower quantities in people with this subtype of depression. The aim of this study is to investigate whether treatment with a synbiotic, a combination of prebiotics (i.e., food tailored to bacteria that can be readily utilized by them) and probiotics (specific bacterial strains that, in this case, stimulate the production of a specific short-chain fatty acid), has an anti-inflammatory effect and whether this has positive effects on the symptoms of individuals with inflammatory depression. For this, individuals with depression and a specific symptom profile (primarily an increased need for sleep, increased hunger, and a lack of energy) as well as blood inflammation markers indicative of low-grade inflammation are identified. In a double-blind, randomized, controlled study, these individuals receive treatment with a synbiotic over 8 weeks, and depressive symptoms as well as inflammation parameters are assessed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Ability to give consent
- BMI between 18-40 kg/m² 
- Willing and able to adhere to the provided diet on the days prior to testing
- A score of 10 or higher on the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale

- Exclusively for subjects with depression:
o Inflammation: CRP of > 1mg/L (individuals with lower CRP levels undergo only the first day of testing)
o Presence of at least two out of the four following symptom categories:
 a) anhedonia
 b) increased appetite or weight
 c) increased sleep
 d) fatigue or leaden paralysis
o Presence of a depressive episode, both first episode or an episode in the context
of a known recurrent depressive disorder without psychotic symptoms 
o Need to be on stable medication for at least 4 weeks or not taking any medication for at least half a year prior to study start. A change in dosage of medication requires a 2-week waiting period prior to participation.
Exclusion criteria:
- History of one of the following psychiatric diagnoses (dementia, bipolar disorder,
schizophrenic psychosis, substance abuse disorder)
- History of neurological, neoplastic, and severe dermatological disorders
- Clearly organic or substance-induced cause of depression
- Pregnant or nursing
- Acute infection (inclusion possible after a period of 2 weeks without symptoms)
- Antibiotic treatment in the past month
- Autoimmune disease requiring medication, at the exception of well-controlled Hasimoto’s
- Intake of pre- pro- or synbiotics in the past 6 months
- New vitamin or other supplementation in the past 3 months (vitamin or supplement intake longer than 3 months is permitted)

- Exclusively for healthy control subjects:
o Any current or lifetime psychiatric disorder according to ICD-10 criteria
